newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia poll body warns against campaign violence.
newsitem.headline: Liberia poll body warns against campaign violence.

text.p: Liberia's independent election commission (IECOM) has warned political parties they could be barred from presidential and parliamentary elections due on July 19 if they engage in violence.
The election campaign began on June 16 and IECOM chairman Henry Andrews said on state radio late on Saturday that clashes between rival parties had been reported in rural areas.
"I can assure you this election commission will not hesitate to withdraw the certificate of any political party whose supporters continue to violate the election laws," he said.
The elections are the latest stage in a peace deal aimed at ending seven years of civil war.
The war is estimated to have killed over 150,000 people and displaced half of Liberia's population of 2.5 million, which has given rise to doubts that proper electoral rolls could be drawn up.
Andrews said the registration of electors would start on Tuesday and take about 10 days.
Charles Taylor, who launched the civil war in 1989, is among the presidential candidates, standing for his National Patriotic Party.

He is reckoned to be the front-runner, alongside Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf of the recently-formed Unity Party, who is a former finance minister and top United Nations Development Programme official for Africa.
